question: How does stock 3.1.28 code put a CJK-capable font on an LVGL v8 label?
prototype_hypothesis: Labels drawn by stock pages get their font from a local style property 90 that is copied off a global font-holder object; the font itself comes from lvx_font_create(family, size, weight).
callsite_evidence: alarm_after10min_prompt (0xc235580) creates a label (0xc347b8c), reads property 90 off the global 0x200a25fc (0xc384e6c), applies it to the label (0xc2bce64), then sets the text (0xc34db6c). German text re-reads property 90 off 0x200a2c1c instead, so the holders are per-role fonts.
0xc2bce64 is three instructions: sub_C2BC984(obj, 90, value, selector). 0xc2bc984 is the generic local-style setter of lv_obj_style.c (its assert string names get_local_style and lv_obj_style.c).
lvx_page_title_create (0xc4f9364) reads property 90 off 0x200a4304 and applies it to its own title label, the same pattern.

0xc355d68 logs lvx_font_create_core / lvx_font_create from ext/lvx_font_manager.c and walks the font-family table at *(0x200a25d4)+28 by (name, size, weight); unknown families fall back to LV_FONT_DEFAULT.
The Manager page built with the default font renders CJK labels as .notdef boxes on Mirage o66.
control_flow_evidence: lvx_font_create(name, size, weight) -> family table lookup -> lv_font_t*.
ownership_analysis: No ownership claimed. The created font is owned by the firmware font manager; the Manager only reads it.
unsafe_assumptions: The family name MiSans-Regular is the one stock code uses for body text (it is the fallback name in the font manager and in the watchface text parser).
Font sizes are not recovered per role; the Manager picks a size and the result is checked on screen.
Static evidence only; no device run has exercised these two entries yet.
recommended_probe: Rebuild the o66 Supervisor, open the Manager page on Mirage and confirm the Chinese labels render instead of boxes.
